requirements.title: A U.S. employer offers a permanent job in the U.S. and will sponsor it: it files the labor certification (with DHS for a Schedule A job), then the Form I-140 petition

assessments.title: The Department of Labor certifies there are not enough able, willing, qualified and available U.S. workers where the job is, and that the hire will not depress their wages and working conditions
Schedule A, filed with DHS: physical therapists able to sit the state license exam; nurses with a CGFNS certificate, the state license or NCLEX-RN; exceptional ability in sciences or arts, as defined
Full-time, permanent job for an employer with a U.S. location, not the worker or as a contractor; if the worker owns part of it, is kin to its owners or one of few staff, it must show the job is real
The offered wage is at least the prevailing wage the Department of Labor sets for the job, such as the mean wage of workers similarly employed in the area or the wage of a union contract covering it
The employer can pay the offered wage from the priority date until the worker becomes a permanent resident
A professional with a U.S. advanced degree or foreign equivalent (a bachelor's plus 5 years' progressive experience after it counts; a doctorate if the field requires one), or exceptional ability
Exceptional ability, if claimed: expertise well above the ordinary in the sciences, arts or business, shown by 3 of 6 kinds of evidence or comparable evidence; a degree or license alone is not enough
The job, as the labor certification describes it, requires a professional holding an advanced degree or its equivalent, or a person of exceptional ability
A doctor from a medical school not accredited by a body the Secretary of Education approves, coming mainly to practice medicine, passed NBME parts I and II or equivalent and is competent in English
A health care worker other than a doctor, such as a nurse, has a certificate from CGFNS or an approved equivalent body verifying, among other things, their education, training, license and English
Proclamation 10998 does not bar immigrant entry for the family's nationalities, or spares them: in the U.S. or with a valid visa when it took effect, an unlisted passport, national-interest exception
A visa number is available: visas go by priority date, the day the Department of Labor accepted the labor certification application or, for Schedule A, the day the I-140 was properly filed with USCIS

dependents.title: Spouse; a marriage celebrated without both parties physically present counts only once consummated
Unmarried biological children under 21; born out of wedlock, via the father only if legitimated as 8 U.S.C. 1101(b)(1)(C) requires or with a bona fide relationship
Unmarried adopted children under 21 adopted under 16, or 18 if a natural sibling adopted by the same parent, after 2 years in the adopter's custody and home or if battered
Unmarried stepchildren under 21 whose parent married the principal before they turned 18

Immigrant visa application fee, employment-based, for the principal, when the family gets the visa at a consulate: always from outside the U.S., possible from inside it
Immigrant visa application fee, employment-based, for each accompanying family member, when the family gets the visa at a consulate: always from outside the U.S., possible from inside it
USCIS immigrant fee for the principal, after an immigrant visa issued abroad, for the permanent resident card
USCIS immigrant fee for each accompanying family member, after an immigrant visa issued abroad, for the permanent resident card
Form I-485 to adjust status, for the principal, when the family lives in the U.S. in a status that allows adjusting there instead of a visa abroad
Form I-485 to adjust status, for each family member living in the U.S. with the principal (USD 950 for a child under 14 filing with a parent)
Affidavit of support review fee, for an immigrant visa, when a relative must give an affidavit of support and it is reviewed domestically

documents.title: Form I-140 petition, filed by the U.S. employer for each worker, with the fee
The individual labor certification the Department of Labor approved, in the original and signed by the employer on receipt; for a Schedule A job, the application for Schedule A designation
documents.note: It expires if not filed with a Form I-140 within 180 calendar days of its approval. The employer may not take payment for obtaining it, its attorneys' fees included

documents.title: Evidence the employer can pay the offered wage: copies of its annual reports, federal tax returns or audited financial statements
documents.note: For an employer with 100 or more workers, a statement from a financial officer may be accepted; profit and loss statements, bank or personnel records may be added or requested

documents.title: Letters from current or former employers or trainers with the name, address and title of the writer and a specific description of the duties performed or the training received
documents.note: Where the job asks for experience or training. If such letters are unavailable, other documentation of the experience or training will be considered

documents.title: For an advanced degree: an official academic record of a U.S. advanced degree or foreign equivalent, or of a bachelor's with employer letters showing 5 years of progressive experience after it
For exceptional ability, at least 3 of the kinds of evidence the rule lists, such as employer letters showing 10 years of full-time experience in the occupation, or a license or certification
documents.note: If these standards do not readily apply to the occupation, comparable evidence may be submitted

documents.title: For a health care worker other than a doctor: a certificate from CGFNS or an approved equivalent credentialing organization, shown to the consular officer or with the adjustment of status
Affidavit of support from a relative who is a U.S. citizen or permanent resident, if that relative filed the petition or has a significant ownership interest in the employer that did
documents.note: Not required if that relative is a brother or sister, unless a U.S. citizen

Form I-485 application to adjust status, when the family lives in the U.S. in a status that allows adjusting there instead of getting a visa abroad

Medical examination by a designated civil surgeon, reported on Form I-693, for an adjustment of status in the U.S.
Form I-485 Supplement J, confirming the job offer still stands or a new one under job portability, if USCIS asks for it or the worker chooses to file it with an adjustment of status
documents.note: A new offer must be in the same or a similar occupational classification, once the adjustment application has been pending 180 days or more
